title: 15-Minute Garlic Butter Steak Bites with Crispy Golden Potatoes
description: Tender, melt-in-your-mouth garlic butter steak bites paired with crispy skillet potatoes, ready in 15 minutes flat. Pure weeknight comfort food in one pan.
story: It was pouring rain against my apartment window last Tuesday, the kind of dreary evening where my brain was fried from work and I desperately wanted steakhouse food without putting on real pants or spending forty dollars on takeout. I cranked my mellow indie folk playlist, pulled out my trusty Lodge cast iron, and decided to make these quick garlic butter steak bites. The first time I ever tested this recipe, I made the classic rookie mistake of throwing raw diced potatoes into the pan with the beef—by the time the spuds were edible, the meat was basically leather. Now, I give the baby Yukons a quick three-minute microwave steam first. That way, they hit the screaming hot pan ready to crisp up in flavorful beef fat in just minutes, while the sirloin stays shockingly tender and dripping with rich Kerrygold butter.
ingredients: 1 lb top sirloin steak (or ribeye), cut into 1-inch cubes
1/2 lb baby Yukon Gold potatoes, quartered into bite-sized chunks
1 tablespoon avocado oil (or any high-smoke-point oil)
1 teaspoon kosher salt, plus extra to taste
1 sprig fresh rosemary or thyme (leaves stripped and chopped)
1 tablespoon fresh Italian parsley, chopped for finishing
instructions: Place your quartered baby potatoes in a microwave-safe bowl with a splash of water, cover with a damp paper towel, and microwave on high for 3 minutes until just fork-tender. Drain and pat completely dry with paper towels.
Pat the steak cubes dry and season generously on all sides with kosher salt and black pepper. Heat avocado oil in a large cast-iron skillet over high heat until it just begins to shimmer and smoke.

Add the steak cubes in a single layer, making sure they aren't crowded. Sear undisturbed for 2 minutes to form a deep brown, savory crust, then flip and sear for 1 to 2 more minutes. Transfer the steak immediately to a clean plate.

Toss the steamed potatoes right into the remaining hot beef drippings in the skillet. Cook over medium-high heat for 3 to 4 minutes, turning occasionally until the edges are golden and delightfully crisp.

Turn the heat down to low. Slide the steak and rested juices back into the skillet, dropping in the butter, minced garlic, and rosemary. Spoon the melted, foaming butter over the beef and potatoes for 60 seconds until the garlic smells heavenly, then pull off heat and top with fresh parsley.
proHack: Do not skip par-cooking the potatoes in the microwave! Steaming them for three minutes first softens their starches, meaning they only need a quick blister in the beef fat to get crunchy outside without burning the garlic or drying out your steak.
storage: Store leftovers in an airtight glass container in the fridge for up to 3 days. To reheat without making the meat tough, skip the microwave and toss everything back into a hot skillet with a tiny dab of butter for 2 to 3 minutes until warmed through.

faqs.question: Can I substitute the top sirloin with another cut?
faqs.answer: Yes! Ribeye or New York strip works wonderfully because of the rich marbling. If you're on a budget, flat iron or flank steak cuts nicely, just remember to slice across the grain before cubing.

faqs.question: How do I prevent my steak bites from getting tough and chewy?
faqs.answer: Make sure your skillet is ripping hot before adding the beef, and don't crowd the pan. If you overcrowd the meat, it will steam instead of searing, turning grey and tough instead of forming that juicy golden crust.
